subject: Re: Intermittent slowdown in streaming chat (production) — mitigation & next steps
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@loganai.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent slowdown in chat streaming — production impact

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing intermittent stalls and long gaps (5–12s) between token chunks on our production chat integration starting ~08:50 PDT. Users see partial responses that then resume; it looks like streaming is stuttering rather than a full endpoint outage. This is affecting our checkout flow where fast feedback matters.

What we've observed:
- ~50% of sessions had at least one 5s+ gap since 08:50 PDT.
- Non-streamed requests (sync generation) appear unaffected.
- Attached is a short log with a representative session (logan-session-0907-snippet.log).

Can you confirm if this is on your side and share any immediate mitigations we can apply? We're happy to toggle client side, but would prefer a server-side workaround if possible.

Thanks — this is high priority for us.

Sam Lee
Head of Platform, LoganAI
sam.lee@loganai.com

Attachments: log (logan-session-0907-snippet.log)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@loganai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent slowdown in chat streaming — production impact

Hi Sam — thanks for the quick note and the log. We're opening an SR (SR-2345) and we've prioritized it with infra. Initial guidance you can run immediately while we investigate:

Short-term mitigations (client-side, immediate):
- Switch to non-streaming (stream=false) for critical checkout flows until we stabilize — this avoids partial chunking behavior.
- Increase your chunk timeout to 15s on the client so transient gaps are less disruptive.
- If you want to keep streaming, enable the client-side reassembly: buffer partial chunks and only display when a 200–500ms quiet window occurs.

Server-side toggles we're preparing (no action needed from your side):
- Route your traffic to a low-concurrency dedicated pool for the next 2 hours to reduce muxer contention.
- Temporarily disable aggressive prefix-KV eviction on your sessions to reduce cache misses.

We're going to:
1) Escalate to the runtime team to check KV cache churn and stream muxer queueing.
2) Provide a temporary routing change and confirm once it's applied (ETA ~30–90 minutes).
3) Follow up with a short postmortem within 72 hours and proposed remediation.

I'll apply the routing change now and update this thread. If you'd like a phone bridge, I can set one up.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: sr_SR-2345.txt (SR reference)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent slowdown in chat streaming — production impact

Tessa — quick internal update:
- Telemetry shows increased prefix cache misses correlated with the periods Sam reported. Miss spikes align with the 08:48–09:10 window.
- Stream muxer queues hit saturation on a small set of edge nodes serving LoganAI region-us-west-2.

Temporary ops we can apply now (indicative steps):
- Bind LoganAI's API key to a warm pool (dedicated routing) for 1 hour. This will reduce contention immediately.
- Increase per-session KV cache TTL to avoid eviction storms for 60m.

I can implement the routing change once Tessa confirms; we'll keep traces and will not affect other tenants. Postmortem will include kernel-level metrics and a recommended sizing change.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary — root cause, impact, and actions (LoganAI SR-2345)

Sam — quick post-incident note and next steps. Thanks for your patience.

Summary (what happened):
- Between 08:48–09:15 PDT on 2026-09-07 we saw elevated prefix-KV cache misses on a subset of edge nodes serving LoganAI, causing the stream muxer to stall while it fetched KV entries from slower storage tiers. This produced 3–12s gaps between chunk deliveries for streaming sessions.

Impact:
- ~47% of LoganAI streaming sessions during the window experienced at least one >5s gap. Synchronous (non-streaming) requests were not affected.

What we did (immediate mitigations):
- Routed LoganAI traffic to a warm dedicated pool (applied at 09:02 PDT) — reduced backpressure within ~8 minutes.
- Increased session KV TTL to reduce eviction churn.
- Provided client guidance (temporary non-stream fallback) which you implemented for checkout flows.

Permanent actions (in progress):
- Fix: adjust KV eviction policy to account for high-concurrency prefixes (deploy targeted rule in next release).
- Capacity: increase muxer queue headroom for us-west-2 edge fleet and add early-warning alerts for prefix-miss rate.
- Telemetry: add a streaming gap SLO dashboard and an automated playbook trigger for routing at 3x baseline miss rate.

Compensation
- We're applying a one-time usage credit equal to 10% of September's hosted usage for LoganAI; billing will reflect this on your next invoice. If you'd prefer an alternative arrangement, let us know.

Follow-up
- We will share the full postmortem (internal metrics + timelines) by 2026-09-11.
- Action owners: Ben (muxer/telemetry), Marissa (routing/ops), Tessa (customer follow-up).

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll keep you updated on the progress of permanent mitigations. If you'd like a quick walkthrough of the postmortem details, we can schedule a 30-minute call.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: rootcause_notes_SR-2345.pdf (summary), timeline_SR-2345.csv
